title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
abstract: arXiv:2611.20218v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior. Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests. We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery. translated_title: SWE-CoWork：将编程智能体作为组织中的数字员工进行基准测试
translated_abstract: 在软件组织中工作的编程智能体必须确定要构建什么、与同事协作，并验证其交付成果。我们提出了SWE-CoWork，这是一个包含101项开发任务的基准测试，涵盖101个真实代码仓库、11种编程语言和12个应用领域。每项任务都将智能体置于一个模拟的工程组织中，该组织拥有26名具有不同职责、有限知识和受控协作行为的同事。从简短的任务交接开始，智能体必须从同事和工作场所记录中恢复分散的需求、调和相互冲突的信息，并实现由私有可执行测试评估的代码变更。我们评估了11个模型，发现部分实现与完整任务交付之间存在巨大差距。两个表现最好的模型满足了约63%的失败转通过（F2P）测试，但完成的任务不到8%。提供完整的信息……（原文摘要被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出SWE-CoWork基准，将编程智能体置于拥有26名同事的模拟工程组织中，要求其从分散渠道恢复需求、调和冲突证据并完整交付任务，评估发现领先模型虽能通过约63%的功能测试，但完整任务交付率不足8%，揭示了部分实现与完整交付之间的显著差距。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces SWE-CoWork, a benchmark that places coding agents in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues, requiring them to recover distributed requirements, reconcile conflicting evidence, and fully deliver tasks, revealing that leading models pass about 63% of tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments.
